# Reserved ruling: scope of a procedural direction

The Applicant seeks an extension of time to lodge a revised costs schedule. The Respondent accepts that the original schedule was served but disputes whether it adequately separated professional fees from administrative expenses. No witness evidence or personal particulars are required to decide this application.

The County Court considers that a short extension will cause no material prejudice. The Civil Procedure Rules require a proportionate approach. Practice Direction 44 is relevant to the form of the schedule, while section 51 concerns the power to determine costs. Neither reference supplies a reason to refuse a correction that clarifies an existing claim.

| Item | Original allowance | Revised allowance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Preparation | GBP 240 | GBP 220 |
| Copying | GBP 30 | GBP 15 |
| Attendance | GBP 180 | GBP 180 |

Permission is granted until 18 November 2026. The hearing remains listed for 25 November 2026 in Bristol. The listing date is unchanged, and the extension does not permit additional evidence about liability.

The parties must use the terms Applicant and Respondent consistently. References to the Court, the Registry and the Costs Officer describe procedural roles only. Any dispute about arithmetic may be raised at the hearing without a further application. All other directions remain in force.
